title: Expenses are due. {boss} signs anything after 4 PM. Your C$38 lunch could be a C$600 'client dinner.'

outcomes.text: C$38, one sandwich, one pickle. {boss} signs it without looking up. Accounting sends a thumbs-up emoji, a first.

options.label: Make it a client dinner
options.cost: A receipt you'll have to explain

outcomes.text: The 'client' was you, the dinner was a sandwich, and the C$600 lands Friday. {boss} signs it at 4:02 PM.

later.text: Remember the C$600 'client dinner'? Accounts payable would like the client's phone number. By 5 PM.

options.label: Round it up to C$150
options.cost: A small fiction on a form

outcomes.text: C$150 for 'working lunch, strategy.' The strategy was the sandwich. Nobody asks.

title: Accounts payable wants the client from your C$600 dinner on the phone. You have until 5 PM and one cousin.

outcomes.text: You pay it back with a note: 'Clerical enthusiasm.' Accounts payable frames the note.

options.label: Get Cousin Vinny to play the client

outcomes.text: Vinny says 'great dinner, great sandwich' in a voice from an old movie. It works. You owe Vinny forever.
Vinny introduces himself as 'the client, Vinny.' Sgt. Bev books you for 'impersonating a client.' It is not a real charge. You stay two hours anyway.

options.label: Blame the card machine
options.cost: A story that has to hold up

outcomes.text: 'The machine double-charged.' Accounts payable sighs and writes it off as 'technology.'
The machine's log says one sandwich. Accounts payable takes it back, plus a lecture.

title: The printer spat out everyone's salaries. {rival} makes C$400 more than you. Nobody else saw.

outcomes.text: Into the shredder. You will think about that C$400 every time {rival} buys oat milk.

options.label: Bring it to your raise talk

outcomes.text: You 'happen to know the market rate.' {boss} blinks twice and finds C$400 for you.
{boss} asks how you know. You say 'vibes.' HR says 'meeting.'
By lunch, three people have quit in their hearts and one in writing. The office has never been more alive.

later.text: Remember the salary sheet on the printer? HR traced the print job to your login. Mandatory Trust Circle training, unpaid.
later.headline: Developing: a salary sheet 'appeared' on an office printer at {employer}. Insiders say it came from {name}'s login. HR has called a Trust Circle.

title: The office printer jammed on {rival}'s 300-page deck. {boss} is standing over it, looking at you.

options.label: Take the blame and fix it

outcomes.text: You clear the jam with a butter knife. {boss} says 'thank you' in a way that means 'we'll never speak of this.'
{boss} turns to {rival}. {rival} turns red. You turn back to your screen.

later.text: Remember blaming {rival} for the jam? The printer keeps a log. {rival} printed it out. On the same printer.

outcomes.text: 'Firmware.' Everyone nods. Nobody knows what firmware is. IT is called. IT also nods.

title: A client sent you a C$900 watch. Policy says gifts over C$50 go to {boss}. Nobody saw the box.

outcomes.text: {boss} logs it in the gift book, a real book, with a pen on a chain.

later.text: Remember handing in the watch? {boss} raffled it at the office party. You won it. Legally, this time.

outcomes.text: It looks great on you. You check it every four minutes.

later.text: Remember the C$900 watch? The client's next email copies {boss}: 'Hope the watch is keeping time!' It is. Your time.

outcomes.text: {friend} sells it on 31st St in eleven minutes. Lunch is on {friend} for a week.

title: {boss}'s password is on a sticky note under the keyboard: 'Password1!'. Payroll is open on the screen.

outcomes.text: IT resets it to 'Password2!'. Progress. {boss} never learns who told.
You now know who's getting a raise. It isn't you. Worth it? Unclear.

later.text: Remember peeking at payroll? IT's login report has your desk on it at 7:42 PM. A day of 'administrative coffee' with HR.

outcomes.text: A C$1,200 'adjustment' with the memo 'adjustment.' The system says SAVED. Your heart says SAVED too.

later.text: Remember the C$1,200 'adjustment'? Payroll ran an audit. Sgt. Bev picks you up at your desk, but lets you finish your coffee.
later.headline: Developing: {name} escorted out of the office by Sgt. Bev over a 'payroll adjustment.' Witnesses say {name} asked to finish their coffee. Granted.

title: {friend} texts: 'Stuck on the N, cover me?' {boss} is asking who's missing from the morning meeting.

outcomes.text: 'Restroom.' {boss} checks the clock. {friend} slides in twelve minutes later, out of breath, holding coffee for two.

later.text: Remember covering for {friend}? {friend} covered your Friday afternoon. And brought bagels.

outcomes.text: {friend} gets a talking-to. You get a 'thanks for your honesty' with zero eye contact from either of them.
Two swipes, one person. {friend} is officially here. Spiritually, still on the N.

later.text: Remember badging {friend} in? The reader says they were in two places at once. HR calls it 'a quantum situation.'

title: {boss} emailed the whole company: 'Thanks for you're patience.' Under it, in bold: 'Details matter.'

outcomes.text: {boss} sends a correction titled 'Correction' and you a single 🙏.

later.text: Remember the quiet heads-up about the typo? {boss} put you on the good project.

outcomes.text: '*your.' Forty people see it. Thirty-nine screenshot it. One is {boss}.

later.text: Remember the reply-all? {boss} hasn't forgotten. Your next three tasks are all 'attention to detail.'

options.label: Screenshot it for the group chat

outcomes.text: The group chat loses its mind. {boss} never knows. Probably.

title: New title, new desk. Whoever sat here before left an envelope marked 'petty cash': C$300.

outcomes.text: Accounts thanks you with a form. It's three pages. You fill it in proudly.
C$300 in your pocket, a promotion on your door. Big week.

later.text: Remember the petty cash envelope? Accounts found the log. The last line: 'C$300, to see who keeps it.' It was a test.

options.label: Buy the team bagels with it

outcomes.text: Thirty bagels, four schmears. Nobody asks where the money came from. A leader is born.

title: New hire {newhire} deleted the shared drive: 'Don't tell {boss}!' Only you know there's a backup.

outcomes.text: Click, wait, click. Everything's back. {newhire} looks at you like you invented the internet.

later.text: Remember restoring the shared drive? {newhire} told the whole office you saved the quarter.

options.label: Restore it, take a bow
options.riskWhy: New hires talk at happy hour

outcomes.text: You tell {boss} you 'caught a system failure.' {newhire} watches you take a bow.

later.text: Remember the drive you 'saved'? {newhire} told {boss} the real story at happy hour. Two drinks in. Every detail.

outcomes.text: {newhire} gets a 'learning moment' in the glass room. You get to watch. It's a lot.

title: {coworker} found the email where you took their credit. They'll delete it for C$500, or send it to everyone.

options.label: Send it yourself, with an apology

outcomes.text: 'I took {coworker}'s idea. Sorry.' Reply-all is silent, then one 'respect.' {coworker} looks almost disappointed.

options.label: Pay the C$500
options.riskWhy: People who sell secrets sell twice

outcomes.text: C$500 changes hands by the vending machine. {coworker} deletes it in front of you. 'Pleasure.'
You find {coworker}'s fake sick day on social media. Now you both have a finger on a button.

later.text: Remember the dirt you dug up on {coworker}? You both hit send at 9:01. The office now has two scandals and one group chat.

title: Closing time at Grind & Gossip: C$640 in the tip jar. Kendall left early. Bashir wants a fair split.

outcomes.text: Three neat piles. Bashir fist-bumps you. Kendall's pile goes in an envelope with a smiley face.

options.label: Skim C$200 off the top first

outcomes.text: C$200 into your apron, then three neat piles. Bashir counts his twice.

later.text: Remember the light tip jar? Bashir counted the card tips against the till. He won't look at you on the line.

outcomes.text: Left early, gets nothing. Bashir shrugs and pockets his half.

later.text: Remember cutting Kendall out of the tips? Kendall checked the café camera. Now the whole floor knows.

title: Skyler Beta wants growth 'up and to the right' for investors by noon. It's flat. {boss}: 'Make it pop.'

outcomes.text: The chart is flat. Skyler Beta calls it 'a plateau of opportunity' and announces a fifth pivot.

options.label: Make it pop (with made-up numbers)
options.cost: Fake numbers in front of investors

outcomes.text: Up and to the right, like a ski jump. The investors clap. Your C$800 bonus arrives with a rocket emoji.

later.text: Remember the chart that popped? An investor asked for the raw numbers. Pivotly is pivoting again, and you're why.
later.headline: BREAKING: Pivotly's growth chart was 'directional,' sources tell me. Insiders point to {name}. The company calls it 'a fifth pivot.'

outcomes.text: Every number is real. The chart is a lie. Skyler Beta calls you 'a storyteller' and approves C$300.

title: The celebrity interview fell through an hour before air. Vivian wants a quote anyway. Jax says nobody checks.

outcomes.text: The segment runs short. Vivian fills it with a weather joke. Nour tells you it was the right call, quietly.

options.label: Write a quote yourself
options.cost: Putting words in a real mouth

outcomes.text: 'Astoria is my spiritual home,' the celebrity 'said.' The clip does numbers.

later.text: Remember the made-up quote? The celebrity's publicist called Clout TV. Vivian says it was your idea. It was.
later.headline: Developing: a Clout TV quote 'from a celebrity' was, we're told, written by {name}. The celebrity's publicist: 'Astoria? Who?'

outcomes.text: Jax writes something about 'loving bagels.' Your name isn't on it, which was the point.

title: Year-end: C$2,000 left in the ribbon-cutting budget. Marvin: 'Use it or lose it.' Nothing needs cutting.

options.label: Give it back to the city
options.riskWhy: Returning money is unusual, not risky

outcomes.text: Marvin fills in a form called 'Money Back (Rare).' It hasn't been used since 1994.

later.text: Remember returning the ribbon money? Papa-Dani thanked 'one honest intern' in a speech. No name. Everyone knew.

options.label: Cut a ribbon on your own stoop
options.cost: Spending the city's money on you

outcomes.text: A brass band, giant scissors, your stoop. Papa-Dani sends a video. The neighbors are confused but moved.
Your cousin invoices C$2,000 of 'premium ceremonial ribbon' and sends you C$1,500. The ribbon arrives. It's short.

later.text: Remember the C$2,000 of ribbon from your cousin? The city auditor measured it: eleven feet. Sgt. Bev would like a word.
later.headline: Developing: {name} sold the Mayor's Office C$2,000 of ribbon. Auditors measured it: eleven feet. Papa-Dani, on the record: 'I love a ribbon.'

title: Tyce: under 1,000 viewers by Friday means the basement booth. A guy sells 1,000 'viewers' for C$400.

outcomes.text: 212 people, all real, one of them your aunt. Chat asks about your cat for an hour. You love them.
1,000 'viewers' who never blink and never chat. Tyce gives you a thumbs-up from the hot tub.

later.text: Remember the 1,000 'viewers'? The platform's bot sweep took them back, and your partner badge with them. Dante clipped it.

outcomes.text: Lulu sends 800 real people your way. Real ones chat. Bots never asked about your cat.

title: A C$2,500 sample dress 'went missing.' Saskia's tote looks dress-shaped. Valentina is counting.

outcomes.text: Saskia gets 'a conversation.' The dress comes back with a wine stain and no apology.
Saskia sends C$800 with the note 'dress money lol.' You're in it now.

later.text: Remember Saskia's dress-shaped tote? The sample turned up on a resale app. Your transfer note: 'dress money lol.'
later.headline: Developing: a missing C$2,500 Atelier Vernon sample turned up for resale. Insiders say {name} got a cut. Madame Vernon: 'Tacky.'

outcomes.text: Valentina docks everyone. Saskia buys the team coffee. With what money, nobody asks.

title: The 31st St '1BR' is a closet facing a wall. {boss} wants 'aspirational' photos. C$600 if it rents today.

outcomes.text: 'Cozy. Very cozy. Has a wall.' Nobody calls. Inez says it's the best listing she's ever read.
Skyline views, a soaking tub, a terrace. None of it is there. It rents in nine minutes.

later.text: Remember the 'aspirational' listing? The renters showed up with a mover and a lawyer. Lorraine takes your commission and your parking spot.

options.label: Wide-angle lens, no lies
options.cost: Bending a room that doesn't bend

outcomes.text: Every photo is of this apartment. Spiritually it's a different apartment. It rents, at a smaller fee.

title: Anjali whispers that Conrad is buying Astoria Pickle Works tomorrow. The stock is C$4 today. You have savings.

outcomes.text: Compliance thanks you with a tote bag. Anjali gets a stern email and a new password.
You buy at C$4. Conrad buys the company at C$9. You make C$2,500 and a new hobby: refreshing the news.

later.text: Remember the pickle stock you bought the day before the deal? Two people in identical suits are in the lobby, asking for you.

options.label: Tip off your crew instead
options.get: Your crew thinks you're a genius

outcomes.text: Your crew buys pickles. Your crew makes money. Your crew sends you a pickle emoji every hour.

title: Two City Trading Commission agents are in the lobby, asking for you by name. They brought pickles.

outcomes.text: They take the money and a written apology. They keep the pickles.
They thank you and write it down. Anjali hasn't spoken to you since. Neither has the coffee machine.
'I plead the pickle.' Nobody knows what it means. They leave, confused. It worked?
Sgt. Bev holds you two hours for 'being weird with officials.' She shares her pickles.

title: Your client's files hold a memo that sinks their case. Mr. Hale: 'Discovery is a state of mind.'

outcomes.text: You lose the motion and keep your license. Margaret sends one line from the airport: 'Proud of you.'
The memo becomes confetti. The client wins. Mr. Hale sends a C$1,500 bonus and a cigar you won't smoke.

later.text: Remember the memo in the shredder? The other side had a copy. The judge said 'sanctions' four times. Sgt. Bev walks you out, politely.
later.headline: Developing: a Whitlock & Hale memo went through a shredder, we're told, and {name} was holding it. The judge said 'sanctions' four times.

outcomes.text: PRIVILEGED, in red, three times. It feels legal. Mr. Hale approves C$600.

later.text: Remember stamping that memo 'privileged'? The judge read it. 'Privileged' is not what she called it.
